simple.meaning: עַזָּה (ʻAzzâh) appears 21 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with flocks.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 7 more, beginning at Genesis 10:19. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, land, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עַזָּה (H5804) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows עַזָּה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: עַזָּה (ʻAzzâh) / H5804 is tracked through Genesis 10:19, Deuteronomy 2:23, Joshua 10:41, Joshua 11:22. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: The border of the Canaanites was from Sidon—as you go toward Gerar—to Gaza—as you go toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim—to Lasha.
Then the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza: the Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed them and lived in their place.)
Joshua struck them from Kadesh Barnea even to Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, even to Gibeon.
There were none of the Anakim left in the land of the children of Israel. Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, did some remain.
Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages; to the brook of Egypt, and the great sea with its coastline.
Also Judah took Gaza with its border, and Ashkelon with its border, and Ekron with its border.
They encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the earth, until you come to Gaza. They left no sustenance in Israel, and no sheep, ox, or donkey.
Samson went to Gaza, and saw there a prostitute, and went in to her.
The Philistines laid hold on him and put out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza and bound him with fetters of bronze; and he ground at the mill in the prison.
These are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering to Yahweh: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;
But now Yahweh my God has given me rest on every side. There is no enemy and no evil occurrence.
He struck the Philistines to Gaza and its borders, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.
Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with its towns; Shechem also and its towns, to Azzah and its towns;
and all the mixed people, and all the kings of the land of Uz, all the kings of the Philistines, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.
Baldness has come on Gaza;
Yahweh says:
but I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza,
For Gaza will be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation. They will drive out Ashdod at noonday, and Ekron will be rooted up.
Ashkelon will see it, and fear;

definitions.full: H5804. Azzah עַזָּה proper name, of a location Gaza , Γαζα (Assyrian –azzutu , etc., COT i. 97 Dl Pa 290, Tel Amarna –azati, Azzati Wkl 38 *; Egyptian Ga¼atu WMM As.u.Eur.87, 96, 159, 392 ; ᵐ5 Γαζα , so Josephus Ant.xiii.5 ,5, etc.; Herod. ii, 159 ; iii. 5 Κάδυτις ); — Philistine city (modern , Ghazze, Razze), approximately Latitude 31 degrees; 3 minutes North, Longitude 34 degrees 28 minutes East, approximately 50 miles west-southwest from Jerusalem, near the sea (Rob BR ii. 36 ff. GASm Geogr. 181 ff. Buhl Geogr. 190 f. ), Judg 16:1 , 21 (both עַזָּ֑תָה ), southernmost of the famous five cities, Gen 10:19 (J), Judg 6:4 ; 1Kin 5:4 ; 2Kin 18:8 , compare Deut 2:23 ; Josh 10:41 (D); also 11:22 (D), 15:47 (P), Judg 1:18 ; 1Sam 6:17 ; Amos 1:6-7 , Zeph 2:4 ; Jer 25:20 ; 47:1 , 5 ; Zech 9:5 (twice in verse); — On commercial importance see DHM B und S 989 Gatt ZPV vii (1884), 1ff., 293 ff.; viii (1885), 69 ff., 179 ff . — For עַזָּה 1Chr 7:28 van d. H., read עַיָּה Baer Ginsb (q. v.), Be Oettli Kau Kit Hpt .; see עַי .
